target_customer: Consumers in Metro Manila ordering food delivery through apps and its own channels
problem: Restaurants carry heavy rent, dining space and wait staff costs. MadEats ran delivery-only food brands from its own ghost kitchens to spend more on food and delivery.
business_model: Own-brand ghost kitchen restaurant group selling through delivery apps and direct

founders.name: Keisha Lao
founders.background_notes: All three founders are women, per e27 coverage.

competitors.name: GrabKitchen Philippines
competitors.what: Shared cloud kitchens hosting delivery-only brands, first branch Makati Feb 2020, more branches in 2021
competitors.traction_then: Branches in Makati, Sampaloc, Malate and Paranaque with up to 15 brands in one

competitors.name: Kraver's Canteen
competitors.what: Cloud kitchen operator partnering with Grab to open GrabKitchens

technical_complexity.rationale: Operations heavy rather than technical: kitchen setup, menu design and delivery app listings.

defensibility.rationale: Food brands and kitchens are easy to copy, and Grab was already running shared cloud kitchens.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Grab opened its own cloud kitchens in the Philippines from 2020; no source found on a direct copy of MadEats brands.

market_need_then: Pandemic lockdowns in 2020 and 2021 pushed Philippine diners to delivery, and e27 and Inquirer coverage discussed rising cloud kitchen interest.

identity.voice_and_tone: Describes itself as an on-demand online restaurant group built for delivery

branding.brand_signature: Consumer food brands under the group, such as Fried Nice and Dot Coffee
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch, Tatler Asia, Esquire Philippines and e27 on its food brands, mostly as startup news.

brand_strength.rationale: Some lifestyle press for Fried Nice, but no evidence of a broad consumer following; the umbrella name was secondary to the sub brands.

outcome_analysis: MadEats raised a pre-seed in late 2020 led by Tinder co-founder Justin Mateen, joined YC in summer 2021, and closed a 1.7 million dollar seed in April 2022. YC lists it as acquired but no acquirer, date or price is public, and the storefront showed an opening soon banner. The cause or terms of the exit are not public, so no factors are assigned.
notes: YC marks Acquired; no acquirer found. Exit type unknown. Lead investors for the seed differ across outlets (TechCrunch, e27, StartupIntros). Total raised per CB Insights 1.83M including pre-seed and YC money, unverified. A trademark search returned an unrelated US company named Mad Eats LLC.
